speaker_role: student (recent college applicant sharing personal experience)
key_insights: States that admissions decisions for regular applicants are typically based on the transcript through end of junior year (spring semester), with senior-year courses shown as planned rather than graded
Says a single B senior year won't jeopardize admission for an otherwise strong student, but failing multiple senior classes could
Recommends contacting the school registrar in summer (by August, safely by September) to confirm how official transcripts get sent, since staff get overwhelmed once fall applications open

Recommends two teacher letters of recommendation (one from a coach/activity mentor, one academic) from people who genuinely know the student, plus asking a month ahead and following up two weeks before, with a backup recommender in reserve

On test scores: even post-pandemic test-optional policies, recommends sending a strong score (states her own threshold impression of ~1300+ as clearly worth sending) since scores can help even if not required, though this is personal opinion not policy
Recommends listing activities/achievements in order from most to least impressive since readers may not read the whole list
Describes the application profile process (parent info, education history, activities with hours/years, essay, university-specific questions) and encourages completing optional fields like resumes
States being a 'well-rounded' straight-A student with strong rank alone is not sufficient at some schools; cites personal anecdote of friends with top-6% rank not being admitted
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker's personal SAT score cited as 1330, taken once
Speaker personally suggests sending SAT scores above ~1300, not sending below ~1200 (personal opinion, not official policy)
States Common App score-sending fee was about $12 per school (per speaker's experience)
notable_or_distinctive: Gives a concrete practical tip rarely covered elsewhere: contact your school registrar in summer specifically to learn the exact transcript-sending process before the fall application rush overwhelms counselors and teachers.
reliability_notes: Personal, informal student vlog reflecting one individual's experience (Texas, Texas A&M-focused); test-score thresholds and some procedural details (e.g., fees, deadlines) are anecdotal opinions rather than universal policy and may be dated or region-specific.
